steps.name: Library size, PCA, sample-distance QC and outlier verdict
caveats: sample_01 is flagged in the data profile as having a library size ~4x below the median — do not silently drop it; the step must produce evidence-based reasoning for its disposition
With only 12 samples, PCA components beyond PC1/PC2 will explain little variance and should not be over-interpreted

vst requires reasonably consistent size factors; if sample_01's extreme depth destabilizes size-factor estimation, note this explicitly and consider rlog or a robustness check as a fallback described in the report
Do not perform differential expression in this step — it is QC only, ahead of any hypothesis testing
steps.context: Raw integer gene-level counts from Salmon, 12000 genes x 12 samples (plus gene-symbol column), CSV at data/inputs/counts/counts.csv; sample metadata (condition: AD-lesional vs control) at data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv. Single batch, unpaired 6v6 design. This is purely a QC/exploratory step preceding any differential expression testing; no reference data beyond the provided files is required.
steps.question: Across the 12 skin samples (6 AD-lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch), what do library sizes, a variance-stabilized PCA, and the sample-to-sample distance matrix show about sample structure and outliers, and specifically is sample_01 (flagged with library size ~4x below the median) an outlier that should be excluded, downweighted, or retained with caveat?
acceptance_criteria: Reports per-sample library size (total raw counts) for all 12 samples as a table and bar chart, sorted, with sample_01's value and its ratio to the cohort median explicitly stated
Reports per-sample number of detected genes (non-zero count genes) alongside library size
Applies DESeq2 vst (or equivalent variance-stabilizing transform) to the raw counts using the 6-vs-6 condition design from metadata.csv before PCA
Produces a PCA plot (PC1 vs PC2, with % variance explained) colored by condition (AD-lesional vs control) and labeled by sample ID, showing where sample_01 falls relative to both groups
Computes a full 12x12 sample-to-sample distance matrix (e.g. Euclidean distance on vst data) and renders it as an annotated heatmap with hierarchical clustering, colored/annotated by condition

Cross-references sample_01's library size, its PCA coordinates, and its row/column in the distance matrix to state explicitly whether it clusters with its assigned condition group, is an isolated outlier, or is ambiguous
Delivers an explicit, justified verdict for sample_01 (retain as-is / retain with caveat and sensitivity analysis planned downstream / exclude) rather than only presenting the plots
States any other samples that show borderline library size or distance-outlier behavior, if present, without overstating findings beyond what the QC metrics show

plan.title: AD skin RNA-seq: QC, library size, PCA, sample distances
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 12000x13 raw Salmon gene-count matrix (12 samples: 6 AD-lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch), with a flagged caveat that sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median. Before any differential testing, the priority is a single self-contained QC pass on the count matrix: compute per-sample library sizes and detected-gene counts, apply a variance-stabilizing transform (DESeq2 vst, appropriate for n=12 and 12000 genes), run PCA on the transformed data to check for outliers and separation by condition, compute a sample-to-sample distance matrix/heatmap to see clustering structure and confirm or refute whether sample_01 is an outlier by distance as well as by depth, and close with an explicit verdict on sample_01 (exclude / downweight / keep-with-caveat) grounded in the combination of library size, PCA position, and distance-matrix behavior. This is one coherent QC step on one data object (the count matrix + metadata), so it is planned as a single bulk-transcriptomics-agent step rather than fragmented across agents.
